transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Cora Vicalman.
President Trump leaves today for a trip to Asia.
While there, he'll meet Chinese President Xi Jinping
and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
NPR's Mara Liasan reports the White House says Trump will not
use the meeting to talk about the war in Ukraine
or AI tensions with China.
Instead, they say that Trump wants to talk
about nuclear weapons, which until now China has not shown
any interest in engaging in.
So it is possible that this big trilateral summit will instead
end up like Trump's other bilateral meetings with Putin
and Xi, where there was a lot of pomp, a lot of circumstances,
but in the end, no big agreements.
NPR's Mara Liasan reporting.
Ukraine's president says his military's long-range drone
strikes on Russia have taken on more than half of Russia's oil
refining capacity, and Pierre Zelenor Beardsley reports
on President Volodymyr Zelensky's comments.
As of today, we have disabled more than 55%
of Russia's oil refining capacity, said Zelensky.
He called it a fitting response to Russia's refusal
to de-escalate and end its strikes against Ukraine's
energy infrastructure.
Over the past week, Ukrainian long-range drones
have hit some of Russia's largest oil refineries,
including a key facility in Russia's Samara Oblast,
a major refinery in the Russian city of Volgograd,
and one of its very biggest refineries,
located more than 1,500 miles from Ukraine's border.
He said continued restrictions on the speed of Star Shield,
the militarized version of Starlink,
are also preventing Ukrainian interceptor drones
from taking down Russian jet-powered drones.
Eleanor Beardsley in Pierre News, Kyiv.
The tracking site FlightAware says hundreds of flights
have been delayed and canceled in the U.S. today.
That follows Friday's national ground stop for airlines.
The government is blaming work by a contractor,
but says it does not know the exact cause of the outage.
United Airlines has become the first major U.S. carrier
to block unauthorized AI agents from booking flights,
and Pierre's Windsor Johnston has more.
United says sharing account credentials with AI assistants
could expose sensitive information
or lead to unwanted purchases or reservations.
Sidon Dogin, who studies AI and tourism
at the University of South Florida,
says it's unclear who would be responsible
when something goes wrong.
That's a million-dollar question, actually,
but if, for example, it gets the date wrong
or buys a ticket the person didn't approve,
responsibility most probably will depend on what happens
and what kind of agreements involved.
Beyond security, Dogin says airlines
want to keep direct contact with customers
as more travelers turn to AI to plan their trips.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News.
This is NPR.
There are more than 160,000 signatures on a petition
supporting former NVIDIA leader Jensen Huang.
They're calling for Huang's return as CEO.
Some big tech leaders have also signaled support
for the petition, including Tesla
and SpaceX leader Elon Musk.
Spanish officials say a record number of migrants
arrived by boat at the Canary Islands over the weekend.
These are off the coast of West Africa.
As NPR's Miguel Macias reports,
some migrants are spending over a week at sea
to reach Spanish soil.
From Friday to Sunday, over 3,600 migrants arrived,
according to Spain's rescue service,
a record since the first arrival
ever recorded over three decades ago.
Migrants are traveling from countries
far down the West African coast,
such as Senegal and the Gambia,
and spending up to eight days at sea.
Saturday alone broke the all-time record
of single-day arrivals with over 1,500 migrants rescued
while approaching the archipelago
on over a dozen large fishing boats.
The Spanish government declared a migration emergency
on Tuesday following steady rising arrivals
in recent weeks.
Spain is immersed in a political campaign
leading to the general elections of November 29th,
with migration a central issue.
Miguel Macias and PR News Seville, Spain.
The body of late labor and civil rights leader,
Dolores Huerta, will lie in honor today
in California's state capital in Sacramento.
Huerta died last month at the age of 96
after decades helping to organize farm workers.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Trump travels to Asia to meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, focusing on nuclear weapons
Zelensky says Ukrainian drone strikes have disabled over 55% of Russia's oil refining capacity
Hundreds of U.S. flights delayed and canceled after Friday's national airline ground stop
United Airlines blocks unauthorized AI agents from booking flights, citing security and liability concerns
Petition with over 160,000 signatures calls for former NVIDIA leader Jensen Huang's return as CEO
Record 3,600 migrants arrive by boat at Spain's Canary Islands over weekend from West Africa
Labor and civil rights leader Dolores Huerta's body to lie in honor in Sacramento
